description:
Design a finished App Store / Google Play screenshot set from uploaded screenshots. Step 2 of 3.

Returns immediately with a review link while the set is designed in the background (about 1–2 minutes) — then call get_screenshot_set to wait for it. The result is three art directions sharing one set of headlines, each fully editable in the LaunchShots editor.

Write app_description from the real source: the README, store listing, or the app's own copy — what it does, who it's for, and what makes it different. Specific beats generic; the headlines are only as sharp as this.

Either pass set_id from prepare_screenshot_upload (preferred), or pass the screenshots inline as base64 if you cannot run shell commands (keep each under ~1 MB). Calling again with the same set_id after a failure retries it; nothing is charged for a failed run.

app_description.description: What the app does, who it is for and what sets it apart — 2–6 specific sentences drawn from the README, store listing or product copy.

app_name.description: The app’s name as it appears in the store.

include_tablet.description: Also produce the matching iPad / Android tablet set. Counts as a second generation; needs an API key.

language.description: Store language to write the headlines in, e.g. en-US, de-DE, ja, pt-BR. Defaults to en-US.

platform.description: ios for the App Store, android for Google Play.

screenshots.description: Only if you cannot upload with prepare_screenshot_upload: the screenshots inline, each under ~1 MB.

data_base64.description: The image file, base64-encoded (no data: prefix).

set_id.description: The set_id from prepare_screenshot_upload, once its screenshots are uploaded.

style_note.description: Optional art direction, e.g. "dark and premium", "playful, uses our brand orange #FF6B00".

name: generate_screenshot_set
title: Generate screenshot set
